title: Career Roadmap: Video Editor
summary: A Video Editor transforms raw footage, audio, graphics, and visual effects into engaging videos for films, advertisements, social media, YouTube, documentaries, educational content, corporate communication, and digital campaigns.

blocks.text: A Video Editor transforms raw footage, audio, graphics, and visual effects into engaging videos for films, advertisements, social media, YouTube, documentaries, educational content, corporate communication, and digital campaigns.

The role combines storytelling, visual judgement, sound, pacing, technical editing skills, and increasingly AI-assisted production workflows. Video editors may work in production houses, advertising agencies, media organisations, marketing teams, or as freelancers.
Recommended degree
B.Sc. in Electronic Media, Multimedia, Film and Television Production, or a related media programme.
Core focus
Video editing, storytelling, cinematography basics, audio editing, colour correction, motion graphics, and post-production.
Potential workplaces
Film and television studios, digital media companies, advertising agencies, YouTube production teams, OTT content studios, event companies, and freelance production businesses.

items.text: Review and organise raw footage, audio recordings, and project assets.
Select the strongest shots and arrange them into a coherent story.
Edit interviews, reels, advertisements, documentaries, short films, and long-form videos.
Adjust pacing, transitions, colour, dialogue, music, and sound effects.
Create titles, subtitles, lower thirds, and basic motion graphics.
Synchronise audio and video and maintain consistent visual quality.
Export videos in the correct resolution, aspect ratio, format, and platform specifications.
Incorporate feedback from directors, clients, producers, and marketing teams.
Manage project files, backups, version control, deadlines, and media rights.
Use AI-assisted tools where appropriate for tasks such as transcription, captions, masking, and rough-cut preparation.

blocks.text: Year 1 — Media fundamentals

items.text: Study communication theory, visual storytelling, media production, and the history of cinema.
Learn camera basics, framing, composition, lighting, and shot types.
Practise editing short clips with a beginner-friendly video editor.
Understand frame rates, aspect ratios, codecs, resolution, and file formats.
Create a 30–60 second visual storytelling exercise.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Professional editing skills

items.text: Learn timeline editing, trimming, multicamera editing, and continuity.
Practise dialogue editing, sound mixing, music synchronisation, and subtitles.
Learn colour correction and basic colour grading.
Explore Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
Edit a short interview, a promotional video, and a social media reel.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Specialisation and portfolio

items.text: Learn motion graphics using Adobe After Effects or an equivalent tool.
Explore visual effects, green-screen compositing, and advanced colour workflows.
Practise editing for YouTube, advertising, short films, and brand campaigns.
Complete a collaborative film or documentary project.
Build a showreel and apply for internships or junior editor roles.

blocks.text: Final-year focus — Industry readiness

items.text: Complete a substantial post-production project from raw footage to final delivery.
Practise client briefs, revisions, deadlines, and project handovers.
Learn professional media management, proxy workflows, and backup practices.
Produce a targeted showreel for the type of editing you want to pursue.
Prepare a portfolio website and apply for production internships and entry-level jobs.

blocks.text: This is a suggested four-year learning plan where the degree structure permits it. If the selected B.Sc. is three years, combine the final-year activities with Year 3.

rows.text: DaVinci Resolve colour page, scopes, exposure, white balance, shot matching
Adobe After Effects, animated typography, titles, compositing
Adobe Photoshop, thumbnails, graphics, image preparation
Adobe Audition, dialogue cleanup, mixing, noise reduction
Continuity, pacing, narrative structure, emotional beats, visual rhythm

Client communication, feedback management, creative briefs, deadline planning
Speech transcription, automatic captions, scene detection, masking, rough-cut assistance

blocks.text: You do not need to master every application at once. Start with one primary editor—DaVinci Resolve is a useful starting point because it has a free version—and build strong editing fundamentals before adding specialised tools.
A strong portfolio is often more important than collecting many software certificates. Aim for four to six polished projects that demonstrate different editing styles.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Short cinematic film

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate storytelling, shot selection, pacing, and sound.

items.text: Create a 1–3 minute short film or narrative sequence.
Use wide, medium, and close-up shots to build a scene.
Maintain continuity and consistent colour.
Use dialogue, music, and sound effects purposefully.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Final film plus a short breakdown of editing decisions.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Social media reel package

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Show that you can edit for attention, clarity, and platform requirements.

items.text: Create three 15–45 second reels from original or properly licensed footage.
Add captions, purposeful cuts, music, and simple motion graphics.

blocks.label: Produce vertical 9
blocks.text: 16 versions.

items.text: Create different openings to test alternative hooks.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Three finished reels with consistent visual branding.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Brand advertisement

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate commercial editing and visual consistency.

items.text: Produce a 30–60 second product or service advertisement.
Build a clear sequence from opening hook to product benefit and call to action.
Match colour, music, transitions, and graphics to the brand.
Deliver landscape and vertical versions where appropriate.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A finished advertisement and platform-ready exports.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Interview or mini-documentary

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate dialogue editing, audio quality, and narrative structure.

items.text: Edit a 3–5 minute interview or mini-documentary.
Remove unnecessary pauses while preserving a natural flow.
Improve dialogue clarity and balance music levels.
Add subtitles, names, supporting footage, and a coherent conclusion.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A polished documentary with captions and clean audio.

blocks.label: Portfolio tip
blocks.text: For each project, include the brief, your individual contribution, editing techniques, final video, and any relevant before-and-after comparisons. Obtain permission before publishing client footage, and use licensed assets.

blocks.text: Certificates can help demonstrate structured learning, but practical editing samples, storytelling ability, and a professional showreel are essential. Check current pricing and certification requirements before enrolling in paid courses.
A postgraduate qualification is optional for many video-editing jobs. Consider further study if it supports a specific creative goal.

items.text: M.A. in Film and Television Production: film-making, direction, editing, and production.
M.A. in Mass Communication or Electronic Media: media production, communication, and industry practice.
PG Diploma in Film Editing or Post-Production: focused technical training.
M.Des. in Animation, Film, or Communication Design: motion design and visual communication, depending on eligibility.
Specialist courses in colour grading, sound design, or visual effects: advanced post-production capabilities.

blocks.text: Choose a programme with substantial practical assignments, access to production equipment, experienced mentors, and opportunities to collaborate on real projects.
Entry level — Editing Intern / Junior Video Editor
Edit short-form content, organise footage, create captions, and implement feedback.
Mid-level — Video Editor / Post-Production Editor
Manage complete edits, establish pacing, improve sound and colour, and handle client revisions.
Specialist — Senior Editor / Colourist / Motion Graphics Editor
Develop a distinctive editing style or specialise in a technical post-production discipline.
Advanced — Lead Editor / Post-Production Supervisor / Creative Director
Lead creative teams, oversee workflows, manage budgets, and shape production quality.
Alternative career paths include freelance editing, YouTube channel editing, trailer editing, documentary editing, wedding films, advertising, and starting a small post-production studio.

blocks.label: AI-assisted editing
blocks.text: automatic transcription, captions, rough cuts, and repetitive editing tasks.

blocks.label: Generative video tools
blocks.text: creating supplementary visuals and experimenting with concept footage while respecting client rights and disclosure requirements.

blocks.label: AI masking and object removal
blocks.text: speeding up selected visual-effects workflows.

blocks.label: Virtual production
blocks.text: editing and finishing footage produced with real-time graphics and virtual environments.

blocks.label: Cloud collaboration
blocks.text: reviewing edits, managing versions, and collaborating with teams remotely.

blocks.label: Advanced colour workflows
blocks.text: HDR delivery, colour-managed pipelines, and consistent image quality across devices.

blocks.label: Short-form content optimisation
blocks.text: adapting the same source material for different audiences and platforms.
AI can speed up parts of editing, but storytelling, judgement, pacing, sound, visual consistency, and creative problem-solving remain important differentiators.

Recommended target profile
By graduation, aim to become a portfolio-ready video editor who can take raw footage from initial review to polished final delivery.
Your target profile should include:

items.text: Proficiency in one primary editing application.
Working knowledge of colour correction, audio editing, subtitles, and basic motion graphics.
Four to six portfolio projects covering different video formats.
A concise showreel demonstrating your strongest work.
Experience handling feedback, revisions, deadlines, and media organisation.
At least one internship, freelance assignment, or collaborative production project.

blocks.text: This preparation will help you pursue Junior Video Editor, Assistant Editor, Social Media Video Editor, Post-Production Intern, and Content Editor roles, with opportunities to specialise as your experience grows.
